mainText: Good morning. Here is your curated AI briefing for Thursday, November 12, 2026. Google has launched Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a new model designed for fast execution and agentic workflows—tasks where an AI performs multiple steps independently. Google positions Hydrogen as a middle ground between its high-reasoning frontier models, Carbon and Argon, and its previous fast-tier models. According to Google, Hydrogen is 2.5 times faster than the Gemini 3.8 Flash model and delivers improved performance on benchmarks like the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, where it scores 51 at its default high thinking level, rising to 54 at the extra-high setting. Hydrogen is now available across Google’s ecosystem, including AI Studio, the Gemini API, and Google Search. Within Search, Google reports that the model improves the handling of complex, multi-part queries, corrects for typos, and enhances the ability to provide structured visual responses like comparison tables. These improvements in search are largely driven by the model’s enhanced ability to break down user prompts into subqueries, which helps in identifying relevant websites and providing more precise, structured information. Additionally, Google introduced an Orchestrator tool in its Antigravity platform, which dynamically switches between Carbon and Hydrogen to optimize performance and cost. This allows for more efficient resource allocation, as the system can utilize the lighter Hydrogen for routine execution tasks while reserving the more robust Carbon for complex architectural reasoning. In other industry developments, Nvidia founder Jensen Huang has stepped down as CEO and board member. Independent reporting from Reuters indicates that Huang’s departure follows reports of multiple extramarital affairs, including a previously undisclosed relationship with an Nvidia employee and others with individuals named in recent news, such as accused spy Alice Huang and Nvidia Vice President of Health Care Kimberly Powell. CFO Colette Kress has been named interim CEO. The company faces potential industry repercussions, and Huang has been summoned to testify before Congress regarding the national security implications of his involvement with Alice Huang, who has been accused of espionage. This transition in leadership at a pivotal hardware supplier creates significant uncertainty for the broader artificial intelligence market, as the company navigates the absence of its longtime leader during a time of intense regulatory scrutiny. Separately, Hugging Face has released an open-source markup language called LLMON, or LLM Object Notation, designed to provide explicit structure for language models. The developers note that current models often struggle with unstructured context or JSON, which was originally intended for machine parsers rather than causal language models. By using reserved special tokens as delimiters, LLMON allows developers to bind instructions to specific data payloads, which Hugging Face claims helps mitigate indirect prompt injections and prevents irrelevant information from affecting model outputs. Because structure and content are separated into different parts of the vocabulary, the model can better distinguish between instructions and data, reducing the likelihood that it will be misled by user input. Experimental preview models based on Granite 4.1 are now available, along with tools for converting existing JSON structures into the LLMON format. Amazon has released new technical guidance for managing costs on Amazon Bedrock. The company noted that developers can influence their inference bills by adjusting specific parameters such as cache duration, service tiers, and reasoning effort. For example, using explicit prompt caching can lower costs, but the break-even point depends on the model and the frequency of cache reuse, with specific rates for 5-minute versus 1-hour cache TTLs. Amazon also detailed a method for tracking and capping Bedrock spending at the individual user or team level using IAM principal attribution, AWS Budgets, and Cost and Usage Reports. This allows administrators to enforce automated spending guardrails—such as applying a Deny policy when a budget threshold is crossed—without writing custom application code. In the gaming sector, Nvidia announced that Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War IV will be available on its GeForce NOW cloud gaming platform starting December 3.
